newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev drops on falling T-bill yield.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev drops on falling T-bill yield.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,690-1,694 per dollar, down from the morning's 1,685-1,688 as foreign currency demand rose after yield on 28-day discount T-bills fell sharply, dealers said.
* The lev eased to 977-982 per mark from the opening's 974-976, tracking the mark/dollar cross on international markets.

* Local banks kept converting dollar positions into marks through dollar/mark arbitrage on international markets because the mark will become the anchor in a currency board system, to be introduced on July 1.

* The average yield to maturity on 28-day discount T-bills fell to 0.90 percent at Friday's auction from 1.71 percent on Thursday and 2.57 percent on Wednesday, making the investment less profitable than building up forex positions ahead of the currency board lev peg of 1,000 per mark from July 1.
* Yield of floating interest T-bills was also expected to fall after the central bank cut its main interest rate to 35.76 percent annually from 47.28 percent, to take effect on Monday.
* Yield on this type of paper, which is usually longer-term, is pegged to the main rate until maturity and is adjusted each time the rate is changed.
* Banks' lev liquidity was high and pressured the lev after the Finance Ministry rejected most bids at the daily auctions of four-week discount T-bills this week, traders said.
